text:
Asha M: Quick one "); I flew to Tokyo for the Global Summit. Corporate card declined for one dinner and a taxi, so I paid those on my personal card. Also, my partner came for a couple of leisure days after the conference and we booked one extra hotel night on the same reservation. How do I split expenses?
Ben (People Ops): Welcome back! Short answers: spouse/leisure nights are not reimbursable. For a mixed folio, itemize the hotel folio and indicate which nights are business vs personal; attach the folio and a brief allocation note. For the dinner/taxi on personal card, upload receipts or attestations and get manager approval.
Asha M: Hotel folio is a single PDF with 5 nights; business nights are 3. Should I ask the hotel to reissue two invoices?
Finance Ops Bot: Reissue helps but isn't required. Upload the full folio and add an allocation line in the expense form (e.g., 3/5 nights reimbursed = X JPY). If you can get a split invoice from the hotel, Finance will accept it and it's faster for VAT handling.
Asha M: The vendor charged consumption tax separately (JPY). Do we recover that VAT-like tax?
Ben (People Ops): Japan consumption tax is treated like VAT. Upload the invoice showing tax lines. Finance will attempt recovery if eligible; mark the file "VAT included" and keep any refund paperwork if recovered later.
Asha M: I also used a local travel agent to add the leisure night and they issued a single invoice in JPY. Personal charge is mixed on that invoice.
Sam R (Manager): Sam here 1 I approved business nights. For the agent invoice, please highlight the business line items and I'll sign off on the allocation.
Asha M: For the taxi I only have a photo of the handwritten receipt from the driver (Japanese characters) and the amount in cash. Is that acceptable?
Finance Ops Bot: Cash taxi notes are acceptable if under JPY 3,000 (~25 USD). Upload the photo and add a short attestation in English with the route and amount. Manager approval required.
Asha M: OK. Also the dinner receipt is in Japanese and has no itemization (just total). We dined with two clients and one was company-paid. Can I claim my share?
Ben (People Ops): For client meals, attach the receipt and list attendees and business purpose in the form. If the receipt is not itemized, Finance may ask for a split justification. For alcohol lines, flag separately. Manager approval required for entertainment.
Asha M: Is there a specific naming pattern you prefer?
Ben (People Ops): Use: YYYYMMDD_city_vendor_purpose_amount_currency and append _attest or _VAT if needed. Example: 20270115_Tokyo_Hotel_48000_JPY or 20270116_Taxi_attest_2800_JPY_attest.
Asha M: Cool. One more: I have some small convenience purchases (snacks, metro) on personal card. Per-diem vs receipts  what's simpler?
Finance Ops Bot: If you prefer per-diem, you can claim the standard Japan per-diem (pro-rated travel days). But switching between per-diem and itemized receipts for the same trip is not allowed. Pick one method per trip. If you already have multiple itemized receipts, submit itemized.
Asha M: I already have hotel + conference receipts, so I'll submit itemized.
Sam R (Manager): I approve the manager portions for Asha's expenses here. Sam R (manager).
Asha M: Thanks! I'll upload: folio_full.pdf, folio_allocation_note.txt, taxi_handwritten.jpg, dinner_receipt.jpg, travel_agent_invoice.pdf. Any additional tips for Japanese receipts?
Travel Desk Bot: Tip: include translations for non-English receipts if amounts or merchant names aren't obvious. A simple one-line English translation in the notes field is enough. Also, if you later receive any VAT/consumption tax refund, upload the refund notice so Finance can adjust the claim.
Asha M: Great. I'll tag @Ben for a quick pre-check before final submit. :thumbsup:
